name: Pint of View Lecture: Pretty Old Cars of Bengaluru—Tracing Blore's History Through Its Automobiles
description:
Welcome to Pint of View – Bangalore's first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in pubs and bars.

About the Lecture

Why are we so fascinated by automobiles? Why has the love for cars and two-wheelers become such a widespread hobby across the world, and what keeps it alive?

This lecture turns to Bangalore to trace the evolution of automobile culture in the city. Starting at MG Road, the heart of Bangalore, it moves outwards through the many ways automobiles have shaped the city.

We’ll travel through the arrival of cars and two-wheelers, the rise of automotive racing, state celebrations, the evolution of the automobile industry in Bangalore and its environs, and the story of public transport.

Then come the thrills and spills of restoration and driving: the hunt for elusive parts, impossible restoration attempts, and hilarious personal mishaps, thankfully not too serious.

There will be a deep dive into the evolution of Karnataka’s vehicle registration system, before the lecture heads out onto the open road. Because, in the speaker’s estimation, there is no better test of an old vehicle’s restoration than a long-distance drive.

The lecture ends by looking at the challenges and opportunities facing the hobby, and how it is evolving to suit a younger generation.

About the Speaker

T.R. Raghunandan is a classic automobile collector and restorer, steam railway enthusiast, industrial heritage archivist and scale model maker.

He is the Secretary of the Karnataka Vintage and Classic Car Club and the co-founder of the Avantika Foundation, which works on heritage conservation. He is also behind the Museum of Movement, a rural museum celebrating the romance of transportation in India.

A former IAS officer, Raghunandan spent 27 years in the Indian Administrative Service before leaving

in 2010 to pursue his interests in strengthening local democracy, local governments and anti-corruption. He now works as an international consultant, trainer and author on decentralisation, anti-corruption and heritage conservation.

A raconteur and occasional stand-up comedian on governance, he brings together a lifelong fascination with machines, movement, history and public life.

description:

Work with clay while spending time with a curated selection of dishes inspired by the menu, looking at them up close and recreating them in miniature. From soft folds to crisp edges and layered textures, each element is shaped by hand, translating what’s on the table into small, tactile forms.

The session moves between observing and making, building comfort with the material while understanding proportion, detail and finish.

No prior experience is needed—just bring your curiosity, and we’ll take care of the rest.

name: Manual 3.0
description:
MANUAL 3.0

What does it look like when a craft refuses to disappear?

Manual is our ongoing analog culture revival at The Commons - a space to slow down, rediscover fading crafts, and put them back into people’s hands.

Manual 3.0 is about enamel painting. Meet Surabhi, an artist from Kannur who has spent years hand-painting the bold, brush-lettered signage that once covered shopfronts, walls and banners - before flex boards took over. Think Nirma ads, toothpaste walls and playful beedi art. No stencils. No digital tools. Just muscle memory and a steady hand.

Come experience an enamel painting workshop and explore his living gallery at The Commons.

“Some crafts don't need saving. They just need a room to keep living in.”

What's the lineup?
12:00pm – Doors open with vinyl, food & drinks
12:30pm – Meet the artist
1:00pm – Explore the gallery
1:30–3:30pm – Hands-on enamel painting workshop

Come with curiosity. We’ll take care of the rest.

Ajji House by Subko, Bangalore | August 30th | 12pm onwards

Can’t make the workshop? The gallery stays live until September 5th.
